summary: William Dwight Whitney was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Williams College, Yale under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, and in Germany under Franz Bopp, Albrecht Weber, and Rudolf von Roth. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Yale from 1853 to 1894.

William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007) and has served as a professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013) and visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Edward Soothill was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of London. He served as President of Shanxi University in 1911 and became Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford in 1920.

William Erskine was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and studied at the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1787 to 1792.
William Evans Hoyle studied at the University of Manchester from approximately 1874 to 1877 and continued his studies at Christ Church from around 1877 to 1880.
William Frederic Sinclair was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Royal School, Armagh, and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a Sinologist who studied at Indiana University, the University of Bonn, and under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. In 1983 he became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later appointed Halls-Bascom Professor in 1995.
William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge from approximately 1921 to 1925. He later held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1932 to 1969.

William James was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Plymouth College and Harvard, earning a medical degree in 1869, before teaching physiology and philosophy at Harvard University from 1872, where he became professor in 1885.

William Jones was an Indologist and linguist who studied at University College, Oxford and the Middle Temple. He served as a judge on the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William starting in 1783 and founded The Asiatic Society in 1784.

William L. Ames is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned his M.S. at Caltech and his Ph.D. at the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as a librarian at John F. Kennedy University.

William M. Bodiford is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Kansas, Komazawa University, University of Tsukuba, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein, later becoming a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1992.

William M. Gorvine is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his B.A. from Connecticut College and his M.A. and Ph.D. from the University of Virginia, completing his doctorate under David Germano in 2006.

William Magee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia. He held posts as professor at the University of Virginia and taught at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

William Muir was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Kilmarnock Academy, the University of Edinburgh, and Haileybury. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Edinburgh from approximately 1885 to 1903.
William P. Chu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his M.A. at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he also pursued doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

William Price was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary and served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College from approximately 1813 to 1830.

William R. Hutchison was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at Oxford and Yale. After teaching posts at Yale, Hunter College, Wisconsin-Madison, and American University, he taught at Harvard University beginning in 1968.

William R. LaFleur was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies educated at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago. He held posts at Princeton, UCLA, and was the E. Dale Saunders Professor in Japanese Studies at the University of Pennsylvania.

William Rainey Harper was a linguist who earned his doctorate at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale, served as president of Bradley University, and was president and head of Semitic languages at the University of Chicago from 1891 to 1906.
